Detail: All scenarios, parameters, and pipelines are driven by YAML configs with environment overlays; no hardcoded values.
Validate configs and parameter ranges before compute; fail fast with clear errors.
No hardcoded paths or state; all inputs/outputs via args or env vars to support headless/batch use.
Analytics must be stateless and reproducible; same inputs yield same outputs, suitable for REST and scripts.
Every analytic has contract tests and edge/fuzz coverage; tests live in tests/ with clear contracts.
Full type annotations with mypy-clean code; no unchecked Any without justification.
flake8, black, isort must all pass; code style is automated and enforced.
Prefer immutable data structures and pure functions; minimize shared mutable state.
All reports/exports go to explicit target folders with unique names; no silent overwrites.
Never rely on implicit current working directory or hardcoded user-specific paths.
Use LibCST for all non-trivial code rewrites to preserve formatting, comments, and semantics.
Avoid AST + astunparse for refactors due to formatting and comment loss; use LibCST/Bowler/Rope instead.
Bowler for declarative bulk refactors; Rope for project-aware refactoring when needed.
Maintain a complete, versioned stdlib module list (3.10–3.14); do not rely solely on pkgutil.iter_modules().
Never write internal packages (analytics, finance, api, config, scenarios, legacy, etc.) into requirements.txt/pyproject.
Avoid pyarrow, legacy redis, bare 'yaml' in requirements; use pyyaml and vetted versions instead.
Do not use git+https URLs in requirements or pyproject dependencies to avoid resolver and deployment issues.
Use a src/ package layout for new libraries; keep code under src/package_name with tests, scripts, docs at top level.
Ensure every package has an __init__.py, ideally generated to re-export public APIs using LibCST-based symbol extraction.
Rewrite imports with a LibCST transformer that preserves all formatting and only alters targeted import nodes.
Maintain a modern Python .gitignore: venvs, caches, build artifacts, IDE files, logs, and project-specific noise.
Before and after major refactors, create git checkpoints for easy rollback.
Start from a small, well-justified dependency set (numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, pyyaml, etc.) and grow carefully.
After refactors, py_compile or equivalent should succeed for all modules; run tests and mypy as part of validation.
Always: checkpoint → clean deps → move modules → generate __init__ → rewrite imports → install -e → validate → checkpoint → push.
On failure, prefer git reset --hard HEAD~1 or stash-based rollback rather than manual file surgery.

Rule: Keep analytics/ and finance/ as true v14 cores
Detail: Core v14 logic lives in analytics/ (analytics layer) and finance/ (finance engine); treat these as authoritative.
dutchbay_v14chat/ is transitional/legacy shim code; no new code should depend on it; move it under legacy/ as soon as imports are cleaned.
All imports must target analytics.* and finance.* directly; remove any from dutchbay_v14.* or dutchbay_v14chat.*.
tests/conftest.py ensures the repo root's analytics package is used, not a nested tests/analytics or legacy package.
Before moving or deleting many files (e.g., v14 cleanup), take a timestamped backup directory or git checkpoint.
No sneaky hardcoded knobs in analytics or finance; everything goes through YAML configs with explicit validation.
Same config in → same KPIs out. Must work identically in REST, CLI, and batch without hidden state.
Anything touching files takes explicit path args, never assumes CWD or user-specific paths. No magic.
Full type annotations + mypy-clean is the bar, not 'nice-to-have'. Every function signature typed.
Define the API contract (inputs/outputs/types) before implementation; tests encode the contract.
Favor pure functions and immutable flows; shared mutable state requires explicit justification.
Don't sprinkle mutable state; when needed, document why and scope it tightly.
For real structural refactors, use LibCST/Bowler/Rope, not raw AST surgery or regex hacks.
When proposing rewrites, provide complete, pasteable files that fit test/mypy constraints, not partial edits.
Keep dependencies minimal, vetted, and boring; avoid bleeding-edge or exotic packages.
New libraries use src/ layout; for this repo, treat analytics/ + finance/ as core packages.
All big changes follow: git checkpoint → change → validate (py_compile, pytest, mypy) → checkpoint → push.
If things go wrong, the solution is git rollback, not hand-editing wreckage.
These two folders contain the authoritative v14 implementation; everything else defers to them.
No new code lives in dutchbay_v14chat/; only thin compatibility shims pointing to real modules.
Direct imports from analytics.* and finance.*; anything using dutchbay_v14* is tech debt to eliminate.
Test suite ensures the repo-root analytics/ is used, not shadow packages or legacy imports.
Keep ScenarioManager, Executive Workbook, sensitivity in analytics/ with clean typed contracts.
All export/workbook logic takes explicit paths, works from CLI, and has test coverage.
Structural moves (consolidating FX, schema guards, WACC) done as LibCST migration plans with pasteable targets.
